blocks.text: Why does social media trigger feelings of loneliness and inadequacy? Because instead of being real life, it is, for the most part, impression management, a way of marketing yourself, carefully choosing and filtering the pictures and words to put your best face forward.
blocks.contentHtml: Why does social media trigger feelings of loneliness and inadequacy? Because instead of being real life, it is, for the most part, impression management, a way of marketing yourself, carefully choosing and filtering the pictures and words to put your best face forward.

blocks.text: • Online "friends" made through social ·media do not follow the normal psychological progression of an interpersonal relationship. You share neither physical time nor emotional conversations over the Internet. You simply communicate photographs and catchy posts to a diverse· group of people whom you have "friended" or "followed" based on an accidental interaction. This is not to say that your social inedia friends can't be real friends. They absolutely can, but the two are not synonymous. Generally speaking, there are no unfiltered comments or casually taken photos on our social media pages. And, rightfully so, because it wouldn't feel safe to be completely authentic and vulnerable with some of our "friends" whom we don't actually know or with whom trust has yet to be built.

blocks.text: 46. What does the author imply social media may do to our life?
blocks.contentHtml: 46. What does the author imply social media may do to our life?

blocks.text: A. It may facilitate our interpersonal relationships. B. It may filter our negative impressions of others. C. It may make us feel isolated and incompetent. D. It may render us vulnerable and inauthentic.
blocks.contentHtml:
• A.It may facilitate our interpersonal relationships.
  • B.It may filter our negative impressions of others.

blocks.text: 51. What does the author say we humans have been doing to chimps?
blocks.contentHtml: 51. What does the author say we humans have been doing to chimps?

blocks.text: A. Ruining their culture. B. Accelerating their extinction. C. Treating them as alien species. D. Homogenizing their living habits.
blocks.contentHtml:
• A.Ruining their culture.
  • B.Accelerating their extinction.
  • C.Treating them as alien species.
  • D.Homogenizing their living habits.

blocks.text: 52. What is the finding of Andrew Whiten's team?
blocks.contentHtml: 52. What is the finding of Andrew Whiten's team?

blocks.text: A. Chimps demonstrate highly developed skills of communication. B. Chimps rely heavily upon their body language to communicate. C. Chimps behave in ways quite similar to those of human beings. D. Different chimp groups differ in their way of communication.
blocks.contentHtml:
• A.Chimps demonstrate highly developed skills of communication.
  • B.Chimps rely heavily upon their body language to communicate.
  • C.Chimps behave in ways quite similar to those of human beings.
  • D.Different chimp groups differ in their way of communication.

blocks.text: 53. What did Ammie Kalan and her colleagues find through their intensive fieldwork?
blocks.contentHtml: 53. What did Ammie Kalan and her colleagues find through their intensive fieldwork?

blocks.text: A. Whiten's classic study has little impact on the diversity of chimp behavior. B. Chimp behavior becomes less varied with the increase of human activity. C. Chimps alter their culture to quickly adapt to the changed environment. D. It might already be too late to prevent animal cultures from extinction.
blocks.contentHtml:
• A.Whiten's classic study has little impact on the diversity of chimp behavior.
  • B.Chimp behavior becomes less varied with the increase of human activity.
  • C.Chimps alter their culture to quickly adapt to the changed environment.
  • D.It might already be too late to prevent animal cultures from extinction.

blocks.text: 54. What does Cat Hobaiter think we should do for chimp conservation?
blocks.contentHtml: 54. What does Cat Hobaiter think we should do for chimp conservation?

blocks.text: A. Try to understand our sister species' behavior in the wild. B. Make efforts to preserve each individual chimp community. C. Study the unique characteristics of each generation of chimps. D. Endeavor to restore chimp habitats to expand its total population.
blocks.contentHtml:
• A.Try to understand our sister species' behavior in the wild.
  • B.Make efforts to preserve each individual chimp community.
  • C.Study the unique characteristics of each generation of chimps.
  • D.Endeavor to restore chimp habitats to expand its total population.

blocks.text: 55. What does the author suggest conservationists do?
blocks.contentHtml: 55. What does the author suggest conservationists do?

blocks.text: A. Focus entirely on culturally-based entities rather than genetically-based ones. B. Place more stress on animal traditions than on their physical conservation. C. Conserve animal species in a novel and all-round way. D. Explore the cultures of species before they vanish.
blocks.contentHtml:
• A.Focus entirely on culturally-based entities rather than genetically-based ones.
  • B.Place more stress on animal traditions than on their physical conservation.
  • C.Conserve animal species in a novel and all-round way.
  • D.Explore the cultures of species before they vanish.
